thread:
zhen: quick sync on multi-objective routing DSL + runtime stability. caught a few surprises in the sim runs that I want to discuss.
zhen: tl;dr: add bounded utility coefficients, hysteresis, TTL floors, and a degrade path for missing features.
leo: saw the sim diff, some policies flipped routes a lot when region baselines moved. can we quantify "a lot"?
sophia: flipped ~6% of choices over 1h when eu probe latencies changed. most flips were between two similarly scored adapters. churn spiked during cold-starts.
anya: sounds like we need two things: (1) deterministic tie-break + stable preference, (2) soft hysteresis so runtime prefers current adapter unless utility delta > threshold.
zhen: propose DSL additions: - coefficient caps: each weight must be in [-5,5] - utility_delta_threshold_ms or utility_delta_abs for maintaining stickiness - soft_constraint primitive that applies a penalty, not a hard reject.
leo: helpful. one runtime detail: normalization uses rolling min/max. when min ~ max (low variance), normalized scores blow up. add clamp and fallback static ranges.
sophia: agree. also recommend smoothing window of 5m with exponential decay and a fallback static range per metric that can be operator set.
anya: adapter feature surface: keep it tiny on hot path. required fields: cost_micros, p50_ms, confidence, tags, version, ttl_seconds. optional: p95_ms for soft_constraints. adapters should not call external systems on each eval.
zhen: on missing metrics: runtime should give candidate a conservative penalty and mark it "degraded" but still consider it in ranking. never blackhole unless adapter explicitly returns available:false.
leo: runtime cache rules: key = adapter_id + version + tenant + region? probably adapter_id+version is enough. ttl floor = 3s, ceil = 60s. emit cache_hit metric.
sophia: perf check: we measured eval time ~150ns/op in the hot path (compiled bytecode). with 10 candidates avg it's ~1.5us per request which is acceptable. but need to keep DSL small.
zhen: compile-time checks: validate coefficient bounds, banned functions, and static analyzers to detect potential non-monotonic transforms. runtime validates on load and rejects policies that fail.
anya: migration: keep old weight-based selector supported; provide conversion helper weight->utility: utility = k * log(weight + 1). warn about non-linear effects in docs.
leo: telemetry: emit polyrouting.policy.utility{policy_id,adapter_id,tenant,region}, polyrouting.policy.choice_stability, polyrouting.policy.soft_constraint_violations, and polyrouting.adapter.cache_hit. also log adapter_version in all events.
sophia: runbook: if policy churn > 5% in 15m window for a tenant, reduce policy to "balanced" preset and notify owners. automatic fallback rule to prevent customer impact.
zhen: rollout plan: feature flag per-tenant. internal soak for 24h, then staged canary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with sim comparison at each step. auto-disable if p99 regresses by >30ms or cost rises >10% sustained for 30m.
anya: tests: unit parser + bytecode fuzzing, sim harness replay with recorded adapter features, perf microbench at target qps, and an end-to-end canary test against staging infra.
leo: docs: add migration guide, sample policies (latency-first, cost-first, geo-prefer), and adapter author guidelines (cpu budget, cache hints).
sophia: small UX ask: policy-sim should show per-request choice history and a visual diff since last policy version to debug churn.
policy-bot: scheduled soak window: 2026-04-02T01:00:00Z -> 2026-04-02T07:00:00Z. alert hooks to #oncall if auto-disable triggers.
zhen: I'll draft the RFC addendum and a minimal prototype compiler. will post PR today.
anya: thanks all. let's aim to keep the first rollout to internal tenants only and use presets to avoid operator footguns.
leo: yep. once PR is up i'll run more sim replays and sanity checks.
